title: Cache & Batch Coach: Micro-interaction Flow for Console Recommendations
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Design a compact, micro-interaction-driven coach component that surfaces Cache & Batching recommendations inside the Redwood Console. The coach should: (1) proactively suggest a small set of safe-opinionated presets based on route traffic patterns and recent token distributions; (2) explain the expected cost/latency trade-offs in one or two concise sentences; (3) expose a guarded quick-apply path (with an undo window and a simulated impact preview) and a deeper edit path for advanced users. This ticket covers prototype screens, interaction spec, tooltip copy, and handoff assets for engineering and PM review. Success metrics: reduce time-to-optimal-config for new routes by 30% (measured in Simulation Lab), and fewer rollback actions after canary rollouts by 20% over the next quarter.
comments: 2026-02-21 - Ava Martinez: Kickoff: aligned with PM on using low-friction coach rather than a full wizard. Primary user personas: platform engineers (fast-config) + product engineers (advanced tuning).
2026-02-24 - Priya Singh (PM): Reviewed initial concept. Asked that we include a simulated cost delta of 'last 7 days' traffic and an accessibility pass for the tooltip flows.

2026-02-27 - Marcus Lee (Eng): Feasibility: quick-apply requires server-side safe-op flag and a 10-minute undo TTL. Suggests adding telemetry hook 'coach_applied' and 'coach_undone'. Also warns about KV-cache invalidation for prefix-presets.

2026-03-02 - User Research (notes): 6 participants (internal). Findings: prefer single-line rationale + one clickable 'Why this suggestion?' that expands. Confusion when both batch size and prefix cache are recommended together — need a combined explanation card.
2026-03-04 - Ava Martinez: Iteration: created 'combined explanation card' with micro-visualization showing request vs cached token flow. Reduced copy length to two bullets per suggestion.

2026-03-06 - Liam O'Connor: Engineering review: added constraints for canary-only initial application and flagged metrics to monitor (p50 latency, tokens/saved, error-rate). Requested API contract example for simulator endpoint.

2026-03-08 - Design Review: 3 changes requested by Design Lead: increase hit target visibility, add contrast to quick-apply CTA, and include hover state for undo timer visual. Liam to action feasibility for hover animation cost.
2026-03-10 - Priya Singh (PM): Ready for final UX review with Growth and Ops. Please attach final Figma frames and copybook. QA checklist added to acceptance criteria.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype implements coach in two sizes (compact ribbon + expanded pane) and is clickable from route detail page
Coach shows at most 3 ranked suggestions with concise rationale and estimated cost/latency delta
Quick-apply path triggers a canary apply (engineer-configurable), shows simulated impact within the UI, and exposes a 10-minute undo action
Telemetry events emitted for coach impressions, suggestion clicks, applies, and undos
Accessibility: all coach controls reachable by keyboard and pass basic contrast and screen-reader checks
Design handoff includes Figma components, copybook, and a short dev-runbook describing undo TTL and monitoring hooks
